description: Locale resolution cases shared by every Hotlayout reader (schema 9.1.0). `requested` is the locale the host passed (usually the device locale), `available` is `localization.locales`, `source` is `localization.defaultLocale` (null: the document has no localization). A reader must produce `translation` (the key it reads `localization.strings` with, exactly as the document spells it, or the source locale; null without localization), `formatting` (the locale for dates and numbers in canonical BCP 47 spelling; null: nobody named a language, use the device locale) and `direction` (what the platform's CLDR data says about `directionLocale`). `formatting` is the longest prefix of the requested tag that is a well-formed BCP 47 tag (`ja_JP_JP` gives `ja-JP`), `directionLocale` is the canonical spelling of the language of the text that is shown (`ks_IN` in the document gives `ks-IN`). A row marked `readerOnly: true` uses a document language that the document schema does not allow (`LocaleTag` is two letters and an optional region, so `zh-Hant` cannot be built in the builder); such a document can only come from another producer, and the row is a rule for readers, not a promise of the builder.

cases.name: exact match
region is dropped: ar-EG finds ar
underscore is a hyphen: ar_EG
case does not matter: AR-eg
surrounding spaces are trimmed
pt-BR with pt and pt-PT available takes pt, never the sibling region
pt-BR with only pt-PT available is not a match
no guessing downwards: ar asked, only ar-EG available
regional key in the document, exact match
regional key in the document, host spells it pt_br
document key is compared case-insensitively and returned as the document spells it
script and region: zh-Hant-TW finds zh-Hant before zh
two steps: zh-Hant-TW finds zh
KNOWN LIMIT: zh-TW falls to zh (usually Simplified) although Taiwan writes Traditional
kk-KZ finds kk
he-IL finds he, right to left
requested locale is the source language
requested region of the source language keeps its own formatting
source language counts as available even when `locales` omits it
right-to-left source language, left-to-right translation asked and found
no translation: source language, its formatting and its direction
no Arabic in the document: left to right, not the direction of the request
no translation and a right-to-left source language
extension subtags are dropped: en-US-u-ca-gregory finds en-US
extension subtags are dropped down to the language
empty locale: source language
no locale at all: source language
malformed locale (empty subtag): source language
malformed locale (not a language tag): source language
private-use tag is not a language: source language
document without localization: the host's locale formats and gives the direction
document without localization, nobody asked: device locale, left to right
formatting locale is well-formed: ja_JP_JP (a Java/Android locale) formats as ja-JP
formatting locale is well-formed: a dangling extension singleton is dropped (ar-EG-u)
formatting locale is well-formed: a repeated region is dropped (ar-EG-EG)
no localization: the host locale is still made well-formed (en-US-u)
direction is asked for the canonical spelling of the document key: ks_IN
a tag longer than 100 characters is not a language tag
